sources.title: Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS
supports: A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment keeps a synchronous standby replica in another Availability Zone
The standby cannot serve read traffic
Synchronous replication can raise write and commit latency compared with Single-AZ

sources.title: Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS
supports: Failover times are typically 60-120 seconds, longer with large transactions or a lengthy recovery
Failover changes the DNS record of the DB instance to point to the standby, and existing connections must be re-established
The listed reasons for a failover include OS patching, an unhealthy or unreachable primary host, a customer modification, a storage failure, and a reboot with failover

sources.title: Best practices for Amazon RDS
supports: A client that caches DNS should use a TTL of less than 30 seconds, because the address of a DB instance can change after a failover
Test failover to learn how long it takes for your use case

sources.title: Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments for Amazon RDS
supports: A Multi-AZ DB cluster has one writer and two readable DB instances in three Availability Zones
Replication is semisynchronous: a commit needs the acknowledgment of at least one reader
Supported instance classes are db.c6gd, db.m5d, db.m6gd, db.m6id, db.m6idn, db.m8gd, db.r5d, db.r6gd, db.r6id, db.r6idn, db.r8gd and db.x2iedn
Multi-AZ DB clusters are not Aurora DB clusters

sources.title: Failing over a Multi-AZ DB cluster for Amazon RDS
supports: Failover times are typically under 35 seconds

sources.title: Limitations of Multi-AZ DB clusters for Amazon RDS
supports: Multi-AZ DB clusters cannot be stopped and started, and do not support storage autoscaling by a maximum allocated storage

sources.title: Working with DB instance read replicas
supports: Updates to the primary DB instance are copied asynchronously to a read replica
RDS does not autoscale read replicas

sources.title: Creating a read replica
supports: Automatic backups must be enabled on the source DB instance (a backup retention period other than 0) before a read replica can be created
The same or a larger instance class and storage type than the source is recommended for a replica

sources.title: Working with read replicas for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: PostgreSQL read replicas are read-only, and a promotion cannot be reversed
Point-in-time recovery is not supported for read replicas
With no transactions on the source, a PostgreSQL replica reports a lag of up to five minutes

sources.title: Read replica configuration with PostgreSQL
supports: A PostgreSQL read replica is an asynchronously created physical replica that uses native streaming replication
Up to 15 read replicas per source DB instance in the same Region
A read replica can itself be a Multi-AZ DB instance

sources.title: Monitoring and tuning the replication process
supports: The ReplicaLag metric is the result of SELECT extract(epoch from now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp())

sources.title: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon RDS
supports: ReplicaLag is reported in seconds; FreeStorageSpace and DatabaseConnections are instance metrics in the AWS/RDS namespace
The T DB instance classes are recommended only for development, test and other non-production servers
Surplus CPU credits beyond what an instance can earn in 24 hours incur an additional charge

sources.title: DB instance class types
supports: The families are general purpose (db.m), memory optimized (db.r, db.x, db.z), compute optimized (db.c6gd, Multi-AZ DB clusters only), and burstable (db.t)
db.t4g instances are configured for Unlimited mode and can burst beyond the baseline for an additional charge

sources.title: Amazon RDS DB instance storage
supports: gp3 gives a baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s; for PostgreSQL the baseline rises to 12,000 IOPS and 500 MiB/s from 400 GiB
gp3 storage for PostgreSQL ranges from 20 to 65,536 GiB
Magnetic storage is deprecated and new DB instances cannot use it

sources.title: Managing capacity automatically with Amazon RDS storage autoscaling
supports: Autoscaling starts when free space is at most 10 percent of allocated storage for at least five minutes, and fewer than four storage modifications happened in the past 24 hours
The increment is the greatest of 10 GiB, 10 percent of allocated storage, and the growth predicted for the next 7 hours
Allocated storage cannot be reduced after it has been allocated
The maximum storage threshold must be at least 10 percent above the allocated storage

sources.title: Overview of parameter groups
supports: The settings of a default parameter group cannot be modified
A static parameter takes effect only after a manual reboot; a dynamic parameter takes effect immediately by default
A pending-reboot status does not cause an automatic reboot in the next maintenance window

sources.title: Maintaining a DB instance
supports: Every DB instance has a weekly maintenance window; an unspecified one is a 30-minute window on a random day inside an 8-hour block per Region (13:00-21:00 UTC for Tokyo)
The window decides when pending operations start and does not limit how long they run
With Multi-AZ, operating system updates are applied to the standby first, then the standby is promoted
For an engine upgrade of a Multi-AZ DB instance, primary and standby are upgraded at the same time and both are unavailable

sources.title: Upgrading a DB instance engine version
supports: Major version upgrades must be started manually; minor version upgrades can be automatic
Database engine upgrades require downtime
RDS applies a minor version upgrade even with auto minor version upgrade off for critical security issues or an end of support

sources.title: Upgrades of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB engine
supports: RDS uses pg_upgrade for major version upgrades, and an upgrade cannot be reverted
With a backup retention above 0, RDS takes two DB snapshots during a major upgrade
In-Region read replicas are upgraded together with the source in a major version upgrade

sources.title: How to perform a major version upgrade for RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: A major upgrade does not upgrade extensions, and optimizer statistics must be regenerated with ANALYZE afterwards
A version-compatible parameter group must be ready before the upgrade

sources.title: Performing a minor version upgrade for RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: One minor version per major version is designated as the automatic upgrade version and is applied in the maintenance window

sources.title: Release calendars for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: PostgreSQL 18 is the newest major version on RDS; its RDS end of standard support is 28 February 2031
RDS end of standard support: 17 on 28 February 2030, 16 on 28 February 2029, 15 on 29 February 2028, 14 on 28 February 2027; 13 ended on 28 February 2026
Each major version has dates for the start of Extended Support year 1 pricing, year 3 pricing, and the end of Extended Support

sources.title: Amazon RDS Extended Support with Amazon RDS
supports: RDS Extended Support keeps a database on a major version past the RDS end of standard support date for an additional cost, for up to 3 years
After Extended Support ends, RDS upgrades the major version automatically

sources.title: Creating a DB instance with Amazon RDS Extended Support
supports: Through the AWS CLI or the RDS API, an unspecified setting defaults to open-source-rds-extended-support (enabled); in the console the option is not selected by default
With open-source-rds-extended-support-disabled, RDS upgrades the instance to a supported version on or shortly after the end of standard support

sources.title: Amazon RDS Extended Support charges
supports: Charges begin the day after the RDS end of standard support date and apply to standby instances in Multi-AZ deployments too

sources.title: Overview of Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments
supports: A blue/green deployment creates a staging (green) environment that stays in sync with production
The switchover causes downtime, usually under one minute

sources.title: Limitations and considerations for Amazon RDS blue/green deployments
supports: Blue/green deployments do not support managing master user passwords with AWS Secrets Manager
Blue/green deployments are not supported with CloudFormation
Point-in-time recovery history does not carry over to the new production instance after a switchover

sources.title: PostgreSQL replication methods for blue/green deployments
supports: RDS for PostgreSQL uses physical replication for blue/green deployments, and logical replication when a major version upgrade is requested

sources.title: Introduction to backups
supports: Automated backups are storage volume snapshots of the whole DB instance, and the instance can be recovered to any point in the retention period
Automated backups are deleted with the DB instance unless retained; final and manual snapshots are not
Automated backups do not occur while the instance is in a state other than available, such as storage_full

sources.title: Backup retention period
supports: The retention period is 0 to 35 days; 0 disables automated backups; the default is one day through the API or CLI and seven days in the console
Changing the retention between 0 and a nonzero value causes an outage

sources.title: Managing automated backups
supports: During the backup window storage I/O might be suspended briefly while the backup initializes, typically under a few seconds
For PostgreSQL Multi-AZ deployments I/O is not suspended on the primary, because the backup is taken from the standby
The backup window cannot overlap with the weekly maintenance window

sources.title: Quotas and constraints for Amazon RDS
supports: The default of max_connections for PostgreSQL is LEAST({DBInstanceClassMemory/9531392}, 5000)

sources.title: Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS
supports: A point-in-time restore creates a new DB instance and does not modify the source
RDS uploads transaction logs to Amazon S3 every five minutes; LatestRestorableTime shows how recent a restore can be
A restored DB instance gets the default DB parameter group unless one is specified

sources.title: Deleting a DB instance
supports: Deletion protection must be off before a DB instance can be deleted, and it is on by default for instances created in the console
A final snapshot and retained automated backups are the two ways to restore a deleted instance

sources.title: Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily
supports: A stopped DB instance is started automatically after seven consecutive days
While stopped, provisioned storage and backup storage are charged and DB instance hours are not
A DB instance that has a read replica, or is one, cannot be stopped
Starting an instance requires instance recovery and can take from minutes to hours

sources.title: Encrypting Amazon RDS resources
supports: A DB instance can be encrypted only when it is created, not afterwards

sources.title: Working with a DB instance in a VPC
supports: A DB subnet group should have subnets in at least two Availability Zones

sources.title: Password management with Amazon RDS and AWS Secrets Manager
supports: RDS generates the master user password, stores it in Secrets Manager, and rotates it every seven days by default
The secret is deleted when the DB instance is deleted
Not supported: creating a read replica when the source manages credentials with Secrets Manager, and Blue/Green Deployments

sources.title: IAM database authentication for MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL
supports: An authentication token is generated with Signature Version 4 and has a lifetime of 15 minutes; it does not affect a session once established
For PostgreSQL, a user with the rds_iam role must log in as an IAM user: IAM authentication takes precedence over the password
IAM database authentication needs between 300 and 1000 MiB of extra memory on the DB instance
CloudWatch and CloudTrail do not log IAM authentication

sources.title: Creating and using an IAM policy for IAM database access
supports: The action is rds-db:connect and the resource is arn:aws:rds-db:region:account-id:dbuser:DbiResourceId/db-user-name

sources.title: Creating a database account using IAM authentication
supports: For PostgreSQL the user is created and then granted the rds_iam role: GRANT rds_iam TO db_userx

sources.title: Using SSL/TLS to encrypt a connection to a DB instance or cluster
supports: The certificate authorities are rds-ca-rsa2048-g1 (the default), rds-ca-rsa4096-g1 and rds-ca-ecc384-g1
With these CAs RDS rotates the DB server certificate automatically before it expires
The certificate bundles are published as global-bundle.pem and one bundle per Region

sources.title: Using SSL with a PostgreSQL DB instance
supports: rds.force_ssl defaults to 1 (on) for RDS for PostgreSQL 15 and later, and to 0 for 14 and older

sources.title: Building Lambda functions with Node.js
supports: Starting with Node.js 20, Lambda no longer loads additional CA certificates by default; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/var/runtime/ca-cert.pem restores the earlier behaviour, which included the Amazon RDS certificates

sources.title: Using AWS Lambda with Amazon RDS
supports: Direct connections are useful in simple scenarios, and proxies are recommended for production

sources.title: Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC
supports: The execution role needs six ec2 network interface actions, allowed on all resources

sources.title: Amazon RDS Proxy
supports: RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, and queues or rejects connections it cannot serve
A proxy must be in the same VPC as the database and cannot be publicly accessible
For DB instances in replication configurations, a proxy can be associated only with the writer DB instance, not a read replica
Each account is limited to 20 proxies by default

sources.title: Planning where to use RDS Proxy
supports: Lambda functions and DB instances that hit too many connections are good candidates for a proxy
RDS Proxy bypasses DNS caches to reduce failover times by up to 66% for RDS Multi-AZ DB instances

sources.title: Avoiding pinning an RDS Proxy
supports: A pinned client connection keeps one database connection until the session ends

For PostgreSQL, SET commands, PREPARE/DEALLOCATE/EXECUTE, temporary objects, cursors, LISTEN, session-level advisory locks and sequence functions cause pinning; transaction-level advisory locks do not
Any statement larger than 16 KB pins the session
DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned shows how often pinning occurs

sources.title: Working with Amazon RDS Proxy endpoints
supports: Read-only proxy endpoints are described for proxies associated with a Multi-AZ DB cluster

sources.title: Amazon RDS Proxy pricing
supports: For provisioned instances RDS Proxy is priced per vCPU per hour of the database instance, with a minimum charge of 2 vCPUs

sources.title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL pricing
supports: There is no additional charge for backup storage up to 100% of the total database storage for a Region
T4g and T3 instances run in Unlimited mode and are charged when average CPU over a rolling 24 hours exceeds the baseline
The page describes a free tier of 750 hours for one year for new customers

sources.title: Amazon RDS Free Tier
supports: The page describes credits of up to USD 200 and a Free plan of up to 6 months for new customers, not hours of a named instance class

sources.title: CloudWatch Database Insights
supports: The end-of-life date for Performance Insights was July 31, 2026, and its users were migrated to Database Insights
Database Insights has a Standard mode (the default) and an Advanced mode

sources.title: Monitoring Amazon RDS databases with CloudWatch Database Insights
supports: By default RDS enables the Standard mode of Database Insights for RDS databases

sources.title: RDS for PostgreSQL database log files
supports: The PostgreSQL log, the upgrade log and the IAM database authentication error log can be published to CloudWatch Logs
The PostgreSQL log goes to the log group /aws/rds/instance/<instance>/postgresql

sources.title: Parameters for logging in RDS for PostgreSQL
supports: rds.log_retention_period defaults to 4320 minutes: log files on the instance are deleted after 3 days

sources.title: Turning on query logging for your RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance
supports: log_min_duration_statement logs any statement that runs at least the given number of milliseconds

sources.title: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
supports: The properties ManageMasterUserPassword, EngineLifecycleSupport, EnableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, MaxAllocatedStorage and AutoMinorVersionUpgrade exist on the resource

sources.title: Resource types that support Cloud Control API
supports: AWS::RDS::DBParameterGroup is in the list of supported resource types

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28 (installed package)
supports: The installed package registers providers for AWS::RDS::DBInstance, AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup, AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup, AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress and AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm, and none for AWS::RDS::DBParameterGroup

sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 (installed types)
supports: rds.DatabaseInstance has manageMasterUserPassword, iamAuthentication, engineLifecycleSupport and maxAllocatedStorage; rds.PostgresEngineVersion lists versions up to 18.3

sources.title: @aws-sdk/rds-signer 3.1149.0 (installed types)
supports: Signer takes hostname, port, username and region, and getAuthToken() returns the token

sources.title: AWS Price List: Amazon RDS, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices of db.t4g.micro (Single-AZ and Multi-AZ, 2 vCPUs), gp3 storage, RDS Proxy, backup storage beyond the free allocation, RDS Extended Support for PostgreSQL, and the db.c6gd.medium Multi-AZ DB cluster

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: System Administration Functions
supports: pg_current_wal_lsn() returns the current write-ahead log write location and cannot be executed during recovery
pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() returns the last write-ahead log location replayed during recovery

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Hot Standby
supports: Connections to a hot standby are strictly read-only, and data on the standby is eventually consistent with the primary

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
supports: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES sets the privileges applied to objects created in the future by the role that runs it

sources.title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive
supports: Hyperdrive accelerates queries from Workers to an existing Postgres or MySQL database, including ones hosted on AWS

sources.title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive: Pricing
supports: Hyperdrive is included in the Workers Free and Paid plans; connection pooling and query caching incur no additional charge on the Paid plan

sources.title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive: Connect to a private database using Tunnel
supports: Hyperdrive reaches a database in a private network through Cloudflare Tunnel

sources.title: Cloudflare D1: Global read replication
supports: The D1 Sessions API gives sequential consistency within a session, carried between requests by a bookmark

sources.title: Vercel Postgres
supports: Vercel Postgres is no longer available; existing databases were moved to Neon in December 2024, and new projects install a Postgres integration from the Marketplace

sources.title: Vercel Storage
supports: Relational databases on Vercel come through Marketplace providers such as Neon and Supabase

definition.ja: RDS が別の Availability Zone に待機用の複製を持ち、障害のときにそちらへ切り替える構成。
definition.en: A deployment in which RDS keeps a standby copy in another Availability Zone and switches to it on failure.

definition.ja: プライマリの変更を非同期に受け取る、読み取り専用のデータベースインスタンス。プライマリより古いことがある。
definition.en: A read-only DB instance that receives the primary's changes asynchronously, and can therefore be behind it.

definition.ja: プライマリでコミットされた変更が、リードレプリカに反映されるまでの遅れ。
definition.en: The delay between a commit on the primary and its being applied on a read replica.

definition.ja: PostgreSQL の write-ahead log の中の位置。プライマリがどこまで書いたか、レプリカがどこまで再生したかを比べるのに使う。
definition.en: A position in PostgreSQL's write-ahead log, used to compare how far the primary has written with how far a replica has replayed.

definition.ja: 書き込んだ本人が、そのあとの読み取りで自分の書き込みを必ず見られる、という保証。
definition.en: The guarantee that whoever wrote something sees that write in their own later reads.

definition.ja: アプリと RDS の間に置く接続プール。多数のクライアント接続を、少数のデータベース接続にまとめる。
definition.en: A connection pool placed between applications and RDS that folds many client connections into few database connections.

glossary.ja: パラメーターグループ

definition.ja: データベースエンジンの設定値をまとめたもの。インスタンスに関連づけて使う。
definition.en: A named set of database engine settings that is associated with DB instances.

glossary.ja: IAM データベース認証

definition.ja: パスワードの代わりに、IAM の認証情報で署名した 15 分有効のトークンでデータベースにサインインする方法。
definition.en: Signing in to a database with a 15-minute token signed by IAM credentials, in place of a password.

definition.ja: 標準サポートが終わったメジャーバージョンを、vCPU 時間あたりの追加料金で使い続ける仕組み。
definition.en: A paid arrangement, charged per vCPU-hour, for staying on a major version after its standard support has ended.

title.en: RDS: the default stack left running for 730 hours

ja: db.t4g.micro、Single-AZ、止めずに 730 時間
gp3 を 20 GB
マスターユーザーのシークレット 1 つ。RDS が管理するシークレットも通常のシークレットと同じ単価と仮定した（未確認）
アラーム 1 つ
リクエストは 0。Lambda、API Gateway、ログの取り込みは発生しない
バックアップは無料の範囲（データベースのストレージと同じ量まで）に収まるとした
CPU クレジットの超過分、データ転送は含めない
en: db.t4g.micro, Single-AZ, never stopped, 730 hours
20 GB of gp3
One secret for the master user. A secret that RDS manages is assumed to cost what an ordinary secret costs (not confirmed)
One alarm
No requests, so nothing from Lambda, API Gateway, or log ingestion
Backups are assumed to stay within the free allocation (as much as the database storage)
Surplus CPU credits and data transfer are not included

gp3 を 20 GB。止まっていても課金される
シークレットとアラームは残る
en: No instance hours. In reality the instance starts by itself after 7 days, so this figure is never reached
20 GB of gp3, billed while stopped
The secret and the alarm remain

gp3 を 20 GB、Multi-AZ の単価
シークレット 1 つ、アラーム 1 つ
バックアップは無料の範囲に収まるとした

20 GB of gp3 at the Multi-AZ rate
One secret, one alarm
Backups are assumed to stay within the free allocation

20 GB of gp3 each, 40 GB in all

The proxy only. The instance and the proxy's own secret are not included

Only the amount added on top of the instance and its storage

この単価が 3 台分をまとめたものかどうかは確認していない。db.m6gd.large では Single-AZ の 3 倍より少し安いので、まとめたものと読んだ

Whether this rate covers all three instances was not confirmed. For db.m6gd.large it is a little under three times the Single-AZ rate, so it was read as covering them
Storage is not included

note.ja: 48 件。LSN の解析と比較、PGlite が返す実際の位置、プライマリとレプリカのモデルの上での read-your-writes と読み取りが巻き戻らないこと、遅れたレプリカの昇格で書き込みが失われること、API のヘッダーと CORS、運用用の関数（ロールの作成、13章のマイグレーション、notes_api の権限、冪等性、入力の検査）、設定と環境変数、スタックのアサーション 15 件（3 通りの synth）
note.en: 48 tests. Parsing and comparing LSNs, the real positions PGlite reports, read-your-writes and reads that never go back on the model of a primary and a replica, the write lost when a lagging replica is promoted, the API's headers and CORS, the operations function (creating roles, chapter 13's migrations, what notes_api may do, idempotency, input checks), configuration and environment, and 15 stack assertions over three synthesized variants
Type check of src, infra, test, and scripts

note.ja: テンプレート（リソース 32、出力 8）と 2 つのバンドルを cdk.out に出力。AWS には問い合わせない。2 つのバンドルを Node.js 24.21.0 で読み込み、API の関数が GET /health に 200 を返すことと、運用用の関数が知らないコマンドを接続の前に断ることを確かめた
note.en: Writes the template (32 resources, 8 outputs) and two bundles to cdk.out. Asks AWS nothing. Both bundles were loaded under Node.js 24.21.0: the API function answered GET /health with 200, and the operations function refused an unknown command before opening a connection

note.ja: REPLICA_LAG_MS=1500 で起動し、作成、ヘッダーなしの読み取り（レプリカから 404）、x-notes-seen つきの読み取り（プライマリから 200）、2 秒後のヘッダーなしの読み取り（レプリカから 200）、/health を確かめた
note.en: Started with REPLICA_LAG_MS=1500 and checked a create, a read without the header (404 from the replica), a read with x-notes-seen (200 from the primary), a read without the header two seconds later (200 from the replica), and /health

note.ja: RDS のインスタンス、パラメーターグループ、サブネットグループ、セキュリティグループ、関数 2 つ、HTTP API、アラームを作る。時間課金
note.en: Creates the RDS instance, parameter group, subnet group, security groups, two functions, the HTTP API, and the alarm. Billed by the hour

note.ja: マスターユーザーのシークレットを読み、運用用の関数を呼んで 2 つのデータベースロールを作る
note.en: Reads the master user's secret and invokes the operations function to create the two database roles

note.ja: 13章のマイグレーションを運用用の関数に渡して流す
note.en: Hands chapter 13's migrations to the operations function, which applies them

note.ja: 接続しているロール、PostgreSQL の版、TLS かどうかを表示する
note.en: Prints the connected role, the PostgreSQL version, and whether the session uses TLS

note.ja: API を通して作成、読み戻し、削除
note.en: Creates, reads back, and deletes a note through the API

note.ja: cdkd の state と実物を比べる
note.en: Compares cdkd's state with the live resources

note.ja: スタックを消す。インスタンスと自動バックアップも消える
note.en: Destroys the stack, the instance and its automated backups included

summary.ja: 59章のスタックを一度もデプロイしていない。未確認: cdkd 0.296.28 が AWS::RDS::DBInstance を ManageMasterUserPassword つきで作り、MasterUserSecret.SecretArn と DbiResourceId と Endpoint.Address を解決できること。AWS::RDS::DBParameterGroup を Cloud Control API 経由で作れること。先に作ったロググループ /aws/rds/instance/aih-notes/postgresql に RDS がそのまま書くこと。PostgreSQL 18.3 がいまも新規のインスタンスに選べること。db.t4g.micro で IAM データベース認証のメモリが足りること。Database Insights の既定の状態。Fn::ImportValue を cdkd が 11章のスタックから解決すること。
summary.en: The chapter 59 stack has never been deployed. Unconfirmed: that cdkd 0.296.28 creates AWS::RDS::DBInstance with ManageMasterUserPassword and resolves MasterUserSecret.SecretArn, DbiResourceId and Endpoint.Address; that AWS::RDS::DBParameterGroup can be created through Cloud Control API; that RDS writes into the log group /aws/rds/instance/aih-notes/postgresql created beforehand; that PostgreSQL 18.3 can still be chosen for a new instance; that a db.t4g.micro has enough memory for IAM database authentication; what Database Insights is set to by default; and that cdkd resolves Fn::ImportValue from the chapter 11 stack.

resume.ja: 学習用アカウントで vp run net:infra:deploy のあと vp run rds:infra:deploy を実行する。版で止まったら aws rds describe-db-engine-versions --engine postgres で選べる版を調べ、-c postgresVersion=<版> を付ける。終わったら vp run rds:infra:drift の結果を記録し、vp run rds:infra:destroy で消す。
resume.en: In a practice account run vp run net:infra:deploy and then vp run rds:infra:deploy. If it stops on the version, list what is offered with aws rds describe-db-engine-versions --engine postgres and pass -c postgresVersion=<version>. Afterwards record what vp run rds:infra:drift says and remove everything with vp run rds:infra:destroy.

summary.ja: 実際の RDS に一度もつないでいない。未確認: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/var/runtime/ca-cert.pem で Node.js 24 のランタイムが RDS の証明書を検証できること。@aws-sdk/rds-signer のトークンが node-postgres の password の関数を通って受け付けられること。RDS が管理するシークレットの JSON に username と password があること。notes_admin が rds_iam を GRANT でき、データベースと public スキーマへの CREATE を渡せること。notes_migrator が 13章のマイグレーションを流せること。呼び出しの payload でパスワードを渡す bootstrap が通ること。フェイルオーバーや再起動のあと、切れた接続が node-postgres でどう見えるか。
summary.en: Nothing was ever connected to a real RDS instance. Unconfirmed: that NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/var/runtime/ca-cert.pem lets the Node.js 24 runtime verify the RDS certificate; that a token from @aws-sdk/rds-signer is accepted through node-postgres's password function; that the JSON of the secret RDS manages has username and password; that notes_admin may grant rds_iam and CREATE on the database and on the public schema; that notes_migrator can run chapter 13's migrations; that the bootstrap, which carries the password in the invocation payload, goes through; and how a dropped connection looks to node-postgres after a failover or a reboot.

resume.ja: デプロイのあと vp run rds:db:bootstrap、rds:db:migrate、rds:db:status、rds:smoke を順に実行する。status の tls が true であること、role が notes_migrator であることを見る。aws rds reboot-db-instance --db-instance-identifier aih-notes のあとにもう一度 rds:smoke を実行し、関数のログの idle connection lost の行と応答を記録する。
resume.en: After the deploy run vp run rds:db:bootstrap, rds:db:migrate, rds:db:status and rds:smoke in that order. Check that status reports tls true and role notes_migrator. Run rds:smoke again after aws rds reboot-db-instance --db-instance-identifier aih-notes, and record the function's idle connection lost lines and the answers.

summary.ja: リードレプリカは手元のモデルでしか動かしていない。モデルはコミットされた文を順に流し直すもので、PostgreSQL のストリーミングレプリケーションではない。未確認: -c readReplica=true のスタックがデプロイできること（同じリージョンのレプリカに CloudFormation が受け付けるプロパティ）。レプリカで pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() が、プライマリの pg_current_wal_lsn() と比べられる値を返すこと。notes_api がレプリカにも IAM トークンでサインインできること。実際のラグの大きさ。
summary.en: The read replica ran only as the local model. The model replays committed statements in order; it is not PostgreSQL streaming replication. Unconfirmed: that the stack deploys with -c readReplica=true (which properties CloudFormation accepts for a same-Region replica); that pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() on the replica returns values comparable with the primary's pg_current_wal_lsn(); that notes_api can sign in to the replica with an IAM token too; and how large the real lag is.

resume.ja: vp run rds:infra:deploy -c readReplica=true のあと bootstrap と migrate を実行する。rds:smoke の出力で、作成直後の読み取りが primary か replica のどちらから返ったかを見る。CloudWatch の ReplicaLag を記録する。レプリカは時間課金なので、終わったらスタックを消す。
resume.en: Run vp run rds:infra:deploy -c readReplica=true, then the bootstrap and the migration. In the output of rds:smoke, see whether the read right after the create came from the primary or the replica. Record ReplicaLag from CloudWatch. The replica is billed by the hour, so destroy the stack afterwards.

summary.ja: Multi-AZ のフェイルオーバー、ポイントインタイムリストア、スナップショットからの復元、マイナーとメジャーのバージョンアップ、blue/green deployment、RDS Proxy、ストレージの自動拡張、停止と 7 日後の自動起動は、どれも実行していない。本文の数値（60〜120 秒、35 秒未満、5 分、66% など）は公式ドキュメントの記述で、この本の測定ではない。料金は Price List の単価と仮定から計算しただけで、請求を見ていない。RDS が管理するシークレットに料金がかかるかどうか、無料枠がどう適用されるかは確認できていない。
summary.en: None of these was run: a Multi-AZ failover, a point-in-time restore, a restore from a snapshot, a minor or a major version upgrade, a blue/green deployment, RDS Proxy, storage autoscaling, and a stop with its automatic start after seven days. The figures in the text (60-120 seconds, under 35 seconds, five minutes, 66% and so on) are the documentation's statements, not this book's measurements. Prices were computed from the price list and stated assumptions; no bill was looked at. Whether a secret that RDS manages is charged, and how the free tier applies, could not be confirmed.

resume.ja: production のプロファイルでデプロイし、aws rds reboot-db-instance --force-failover のあいだ rds:smoke を繰り返して、失敗が続いた秒数を記録する。aws rds restore-db-instance-to-point-in-time で別名のインスタンスに戻し、エンドポイントが新しいこととパラメーターグループが既定に戻ることを見る。1 か月後に Cost Explorer で RDS と Secrets Manager の行を確かめる。
resume.en: Deploy with the production profile, repeat rds:smoke during aws rds reboot-db-instance --force-failover, and record for how many seconds it fails. Restore to a new instance with aws rds restore-db-instance-to-point-in-time and see that the endpoint is new and the parameter group is back to the default. After a month, look at the RDS and Secrets Manager lines in Cost Explorer.
